title: Совет из больницы  (Advice from the Hospital)

segments.t: Unable to control the kitchen on his own, Lyova calls Chef Barinov at the hospital to report that Senya and Fedya refuse to stop arguing while orders pile up. Barinov tells Lyova to either lock the pair in the walk-in refrigerator or use his head to make them yield to one another.
Федя с синей все время спорит.
Now let's go back through the conversation line by line.
'Chef, hello.' Lyova displays a warm posture for Barinov, leaning on "zdravstvuyte" ("hello") before closing the thought with "shef" ("Chef").
'Come on, out with it.' Lyova displays a firm line during the exchange, letting the single Russian word "davay" ("let's") carry the entire reaction on its own.
'Hello, Chef.' Fedya offers a direct course without hesitation, weaving "zdravstvuy" ("hello") together with "shef" ("Chef") just the way native speakers do.
'How are you doing?' Barinov wonders pointedly in this moment, placing "kak" ("how") straight beside "dela" ("things, affairs") with no word for "to be" needed.
'And how are things with you?' Lyova challenges quietly as the beat lands, pairing "kak" ("how") with "tebya" ("you") to get the point across in plain spoken Russian.
'There are problems in my...' Fedya presents a steady approach for Lyova, pairing "yest" ("there is") with "problemy" ("problems") to get the point across in plain spoken Russian.
'In your kitchen.' Barinov keeps an emphatic mood in this beat, building the phrase around "kukhne" ("kitchen") and "na" ("on, onto") for a crisp, natural delivery.
Федя с синей все время спорит.

'Fedya and Senya are arguing all the time.' Lyova establishes a natural attitude without hesitation, putting "siney" ("blue, dark blue") alongside "vremya" ("time") in a tight, everyday turn of phrase.
'And all the work has ground to a halt.' Fedya sets a measured rhythm at this moment, pairing "rabota" ("job") with "stoit" ("is parked") to get the point across in plain spoken Russian.
'Viktor Petrovich, what should I do?' Lyova wonders frankly at this point, pairing "delat" ("do") with "viktor" ("Viktor") to get the point across in plain spoken Russian.

'Lock the two of them in the walk-in fridge.' Lyova presents a thoughtful angle as the scene unfolds, pairing "posadi" ("to seat, to plant") with "kholodilnik" ("fridge") to get the point across in plain spoken Russian.
'Then use your brain, Lyova.' Fedya sustains a pointed tempo during the exchange, leaning on "togda" ("back then") before closing the thought with "vklyuchi" ("turn on, put on").
'Make them give in to each other.' Barinov shows a steady view without hesitation, linking "zastav" ("to force, make"), "ustupit" ("yield, give in"), and "drug" ("friend") in one brisk exchange.
Федя с синей все время спорит.

That wraps up this scene as desperate to get Senya and Fedya back to work, Lyova calls Chef Barinov in the hospital, who advises him to lock them in the walk-in fridge or trick them into reconciling. Until next time!
